protocol: per benchmark bench_eval --limit L, L = ceil(500 / n_generators): the first L sorted reals and the first L sorted fakes of every generator (bench_eval.discover order), a fixed subset (repro/vlm_bench/subsets/<bench>.json lists every file with its sha1). The same subset is used for every VLM and for the comparator detectors (user decision 2026-11-16: subsampled).
internal_only_note: Comparators whose weights are not publicly licensed (no LICENSE / unclear terms; the keys of synthscope.hub.NEVER_REDISTRIBUTE that are comparators here), restored from the field-report matrix spec (repro/matrix/spec.json on fieldreport/harness @ 2691337). They are scored like the rest but are not servable, so compare.py reports a best overall detector and a best publicly licensed / servable one (ruling T2-C2).
best_tie_break: equal values (rounded to 2 decimals): the alphabetically first detector key is named, every tied key is listed under `tied`
rank_note: rank_<metric> = 1 + the number of comparators strictly better (the VLM among the comparators plus itself); rank_all_<metric> also counts the other VLMs. Best and median are over the comparators.
acc_pooled_note: acc_pooled counts every scored (generator, image) pair once: a real pool shared by several generators (ufd8, synthbuster_coco; bench_eval's shared-reals layout) is counted once per generator, so reals and fakes keep the 1:1 balance of the subset. acc_pooled_distinct counts each image once, so the shared reals count once and the fakes dominate (ufd8: 630 distinct images, 504 of them fake); it is not comparable with acc. The headline acc (balanced mean over generators) is unaffected by either.

veritaspp.decoding: official (T 0.7, top-p 0.8, top-k 20), seed 0 per image

evalgen.metric_note: fakes-only accuracy is our inference (the paper does not say how EvalGEN is scored; its DDA row, 97.2, matches DDA's fakes-only EvalGEN accuracy); balanced_acc is the benchmark's balanced accuracy (fakes + MSCOCO reals) on the same images. Ours is a 500-fake subset, not the full set.

genimage_val100k.paper_benchmark: GenImage (appendix table 'Comparison on GenImage'; the paper JPEG-compresses the fakes 'following BFree' to match the reals' format and gives no quality factor)
genimage_val100k.ours_note: subset (63 real + 63 fake per generator), fakes JPEG q96 (bench_eval --jpeg-fakes 96); q96 is our choice, following DDA's published GenImage protocol, not a value stated in this paper
genimage_val100k.full_method_note: context only, no delta: the paper's number includes the unreleased pixel expert

aigcdetect17.paper_benchmark: AIGCDetectBenchmark (appendix table 'Comparison of balanced accuracy on AIGCDetectBenchmark'; its caption does not mention JPEG compression)
aigcdetect17.ours_note: subset (30 real + 30 fake per generator), fakes JPEG q96 (bench_eval --jpeg-fakes 96). INFERENCE: the paper states the fake-JPEG step for GenImage only; applying it here, and the q96 quality (which follows DDA's published protocol), are our assumptions. The clean run is in the subset rows
aigcdetect17.full_method_note: context only, no delta: the paper's number includes the unreleased pixel expert

wildrf.ours_note: FULL test split (2,503 images), bench_eval balanced accuracy per platform and their mean
wildrf.full_method_note: context only, no delta: the paper's number includes the unreleased pixel expert

aigibench25.paper_benchmark: AIGI-Bench (Table 1: its two in-the-wild subsets CommunityUI = our CommunityAI, and SocialRF)
aigibench25.ours_note: SUBSET slice: the CommunityAI and SocialRF generators of the aigibench25 subset only (20 real + 20 fake each; the full sets are 12,000 + 6,000 images, not run)
aigibench25.full_method_note: context only, no delta: the paper's number includes the unreleased pixel expert

cospybench.paper_benchmark: CO-SPY-Bench/in-the-wild (Table 1: Civitai, DALL-E 3, instavibe.ai, Lexica, Midjourney-v6)
cospybench.not_held: we hold only Co-Spy-Bench's synthetic part (5 caption sets x 22 generators); its in-the-wild part is not downloaded, so there is no comparable number

bfree_online.ours_note: subset: 269 real + 500 fake = 769 images (limit 500 per class; the benchmark folder has only 269 reals); acc is balanced, so the imbalance does not weight it
bfree_online.full_method_note: context only, no delta: the paper's number includes the unreleased pixel expert

paper_note.veritaspp: Veritas++ arXiv 2607.27113 v1, Acc. column. Decoding: the paper's text does not state a sampling temperature; T 0.7 is the setting of the authors' official inference script (infer_vllm_single.py), with top-p 0.8 / top-k 20 from the released generation_config.json, and 'sampled' below means that setting. EvalGEN: fakes-only scoring is our inference from the DDA row (97.2), not stated in the paper; the balanced accuracy is reported next to it.
paper_note.adb_vlm: Align, Don't Blend (AlignGemini) arXiv 2512.06746 v3. The paper's detector is the VLM branch OR a pixel-artifact expert (DINOv2 + LoRA trained on VAE reconstructions); only the VLM branch is released, so NONE of the paper's tables is reproducible here. Printed numbers (full_method) are context, not targets. The paper prints no VLM-only number for the released adapter, so no row gets a delta. Table 4 'Qwen2.5-VL-7B' ('baseline methods under the same training set', retrained on the same semantic and pixel corpora) is ambiguous between the base and a trained VLM; Table 5 'Qwen2.5-VL-7B (Untrained)' is the base model without the adapter. Neither is the released adapter. GenImage / AIGCDetect: ours are also run with the fakes JPEG-compressed at q96 (jpegfakes96): the paper states that step for GenImage only, and q96 follows DDA's published protocol (an inference, see ours_note). Decoding: greedy (temperature 0, predict.py), which is the official setting. The paper's AlignGemini GenImage per-generator row appears column-permuted relative to its AIGCDetect row (the baselines agree across the two tables), so only its 91.7 average is used.
